analysis.title: Microsoft Corporation 1Q27 Preview: Azure growth and a growing focus on the enterprise AI stack
key_insights: BofA reiterates Buy and a $600 price objective on MSFT (price $531.87). The stock is up about 33% since 4Q26 results, which showed 43% Azure growth. 1Q27 results are due Oct. 28, 2026.

BofA expects 1Q27 Azure revenue of $32.3bn, +44.8% YoY in constant currency, and 2Q27 growth of 45.1%. Azure is now reported in dollars for the first time under a narrower definition that excludes GitHub and Security Copilot. BofA's 1Q27 Azure estimate is in line with Street.

BofA's 309-respondent CIO survey puts Microsoft first at several layers of the enterprise AI stack: Copilot adoption (76.7%), planned security spending increases (69.3%) and likely use for cloud AI infrastructure (88.4%).

Azure growth is gated by compute capacity. Microsoft adds about 1GW of data center capacity per quarter, has cut GPU deployment times in its largest regions by nearly 50%, and raised Copilot workload throughput 4x since the start of the year. BofA believes Azure demand will exceed supply through FY27.

Maia 300, Microsoft's in-house inference chip, is planned for CY27 and is expected to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems. BofA expects it to improve inference economics and let Microsoft serve more AI demand with the same power.

The redesigned Copilot combines chat, delegated work (Cowork), app building (Code) and AI agents (Autopilot) in one interface, connected to company data through Fabric IQ. BofA frames it as Microsoft's bid to make Copilot the operating layer for enterprise AI.

Copilot pricing keeps the $30 fixed-price Microsoft 365 Copilot seat for everyday tasks and bills advanced capabilities through usage-based Copilot Credits on top of the seat. BofA sees a credible path to higher ARPU (revenue per user).
Copilot paid seats rose from 15mn in 2Q26 to 20mn in 3Q26 and 30mn in 4Q26, with net additions more than doubling QoQ in 4Q26. BofA says continued seat momentum is needed to support the stock.

BofA models 1Q27 revenue of $90.6bn (+16.6% YoY) and EPS of $4.73, both in line with Street. Agents & Infrastructure revenue is modeled +22.6%, Microsoft 365 Cloud +15.9%, and Devices & Consumers -6.2% on Xbox weakness.

Capex stays elevated. BofA models 1Q27 capex including finance leases at about $50.8bn and FY27 at $220.7bn, up 51.9% YoY. FY27 free cash flow is modeled at $29.3bn, down 56.3%, with FCF margin of 7.5%.

BofA raised FY27-FY29 estimates: FY27 revenue to $391.9bn from $388.5bn and EPS to $19.70 from $19.55. FY28 EPS goes to $23.43 from $22.89 and FY29 EPS to $28.49 from $27.61. Modeled FY27 Azure growth rises to 44.3% from 41.8%.
Into the print BofA will watch whether faster deployment and efficiency gains turn into incremental Azure revenue, and what the timing of added capacity implies for Azure growth.
The $600 price objective rests on 28x CY27E P/E, a premium to the 18-25x peer group. BofA says sustained revenue growth and margin profile justify a multiple above the peer range.

market_movers.rationale: Azure growth of about 45% supported by about 1GW of capacity added per quarter, plus Copilot monetization and broad enterprise AI stack strength in BofA's CIO survey. Stock at $531.87 against a $600 objective.

sector_views.rationale: BofA expects Microsoft to sustain mid double-digit growth over the next three years led by Azure, Microsoft 365 and AI services. 76.4% of surveyed CIOs expect software budget increases, with AI applications taking the largest share of new AI spending.

earnings_insights: MSFT 1Q27 results are due Oct. 28, 2026. BofA estimates (not yet reported): revenue $90.6bn (+16.6% YoY), GAAP EPS $4.73, versus Street revenue $90.6bn and EPS $4.72 (Bloomberg). BofA's EPS estimate sits above its prior $4.69.
BofA 2Q27 estimates (not yet reported): revenue $95.8bn (+17.8% YoY cc), GAAP EPS $4.84 versus Street $4.84, Azure growth 45.1% cc.
BofA FY27 (June year-end) estimates: revenue $391.9bn (+18.1%), EPS $19.70 versus consensus $19.76 (Bloomberg) and $19.70 (Visible Alpha). FY28 EPS $23.43 and FY29 EPS $28.49.
BofA 1Q27 operating margin estimate is 48.4% and FCF margin 9.7%. FY27 operating margin is modeled at 46.4%, down 20bps YoY.
1Q27 capex including leases is modeled at $50.8bn versus Street $51.8bn. FY27 capex is modeled at $220.7bn versus Street $218.6bn.
Reference prints: FY26 EPS of $17.95 (adjusted) and $17.94 GAAP. Prior quarterly EPS: 1Q26 $3.72, 2Q26 $5.16, 3Q26 $4.27, 4Q26 $4.81, all as reported. 4Q26 Azure growth was 43% YoY.

trade_ideas.description: Long MSFT (Buy) into 1Q27 results with a $600 price objective, based on 28x CY27E P/E
trade_ideas.rationale: Azure acceleration, Copilot monetization and breadth across the enterprise AI stack.
trade_ideas.risk: Near-term gross margin pressure as Azure grows as a share of revenue, faster innovation by AI application and model providers, and cyclical enterprise application spending.

risk_factors: Near-term gross margin pressure as the Azure business grows as a percentage of overall revenue.
AI applications and model providers could innovate at a faster rate than Microsoft, potentially limiting its growth profile.
Enterprise application spending has proven to be highly cyclical given the discretionary nature of applications projects.
Elevated capex and falling free cash flow: FY27 FCF modeled at $29.3bn, down 56.3% YoY.
Azure revenue conversion depends on delivering compute capacity, and the pace of AI capacity additions is a key variable for the outlook.
Devices & Consumers revenue is modeled to decline 6.2% in 1Q27 on continued Xbox weakness.

tension_points.bull_case: Faster GPU deployment, 4x Copilot throughput gains and about 1GW of capacity added per quarter let Azure grow about 45% while demand exceeds supply through FY27.
tension_points.bear_case: Revenue conversion is gated by compute capacity, and the buildout keeps capex at $220.7bn for FY27, cutting FY27 free cash flow 56.3% to $29.3bn. Gross margin faces pressure as Azure grows as a share of revenue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Azure growth or the timing of added capacity at the Oct. 28 print failing to show faster deployment turning into incremental revenue.

theme_stances.key_argument: Faster deployment and efficiency gains support continued Azure acceleration in FY27.
theme_stances.evidence: supporting our view of continued Azure acceleration in FY27

theme_stances.key_argument: The redesigned Copilot and usage-based credits give a path to higher ARPU and a growth factor beyond Azure.
theme_stances.evidence: position Copilot as the operating layer and primary interface for enterprise AI
